From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Dec 12, 2025 at 8:37 AM
Subject: Release gating + operational readiness for signed offline bundles (Redwood Private)

Team—

As we move toward pilot (air-gapped) for signed offline bundles, I want to lock down operational readiness + release gating. This is a reliability/security feature; we can’t ship it “best effort.”

Can we align today on:
1) Alerting for signing pipeline failures (where it pages + who owns remediation)
2) Runbook ownership (signing pipeline, key rotation, installer verification failures)
3) On-call expectations during release week (who is primary/secondary)
4) Concrete gating checks for the Private release train (what blocks cut + what blocks publish)

Connor—please propose gating criteria + where it lives in the release train.
Sahana—what’s realistic for actionable alerts (not noise) and dashboards?
Sean—what are you comfortable with on-call wise (SRE vs Release Eng) and escalation path?
Marcus—please sanity check that we’re failing closed + break-glass use is auditable.

Goal: we leave this thread with owners + dates. We cannot rely on tribal knowledge when a customer is waiting in an air-gapped facility.

Thanks,
Neha
VP, Infra/SRE
Redwood Inference


---

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Dec 12, 2025 at 9:14 AM
Subject: Re: Release gating + operational readiness for signed offline bundles (Redwood Private)

Agree with the framing.

Proposed release train gating (ties to ENG-4862):

A) Block “cut” of Private RC if any of the following are missing:
- Offline bundle manifest generated deterministically (bundle build job produces manifest + artifact list)
- Detached signature file present (manifest.sig) and signature verifies against prod trust root in CI
- Integration tests for tamper cases green (modified manifest / swapped artifact / truncated bundle)
- Break-glass override flag is present but disabled by default; when enabled, emits explicit audit marker (we should require test coverage that it logs)

B) Block “publish” of final Private artifacts if:
- Signing step did not run in protected environment (we can assert attestation from pipeline step; we’re currently using the signing runner)
- Bundle verification tool (installer preflight) fails against published artifacts (end-to-end verify test)

Operational notes:
- The signing job is a single point of failure for release day. We need paging to Release Eng on failure; SRE secondary if it’s infra (runner/HSM emulator/etc.).
- We should publish a lightweight “release gating checklist” in Confluence and link it from #eng-releases.

I attached a draft checklist (very WIP) to start the discussion.

Attachment: signed-bundles-release-gating-checklist-v0.3.docx

Connor
Release Engineering Lead

From: Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Dec 12, 2025 at 10:02 AM
Subject: Re: Release gating + operational readiness for signed offline bundles (Redwood Private)

On alerting/dashboards (ENG-4874):

What we can do without creating pager spam:

1) Page on signing job hard-fail only (not flaky test failures)
- Condition: signing step exit != 0 OR signature verification step fails OR key access denied
- Route: Release Eng primary (Connor’s rotation), SRE secondary (Sean / infra-oncall)
- Add “link-to-runbook” + last 50 lines of signing step log in the alert payload

2) Non-paging alerts (Slack only) for early signals:
- signing duration p95 > threshold (e.g., > 15 min) for 3 consecutive runs
- signature verification integration tests exceeding time budget (we’ve seen these run long)

3) Dashboard:
- last N signing jobs: pass/fail, duration, failure reason taxonomy
- “time to re-issue signed bundle” (from first failure to next green) — useful SLO-style metric

One gap: we still see occasional staging runner timeouts when the signing stage uses the HSM emulator. I can isolate this by separating tests from the signing step (so signing itself is stable, tests can be retried independently). That would reduce false pages.

Also: for air-gapped customers, time skew issues can cause “not yet valid” style failures depending on envelope. If we’re using cert validity windows, we should ensure the installer error message is unambiguous and points to the time-skew doc/runbook.

If you want, I can write a first cut of the alert rules today and route to Connor/Sean for review.

Sahana
Build/CI

Date: Fri, Dec 12, 2025 at 10:41 AM
Subject: Re: Release gating + operational readiness for signed offline bundles (Redwood Private)

On-call + runbook ownership proposal:

A) Ownership boundaries
- Release Eng owns: signing job correctness, release gating checklist, key ceremony coordination (with Security), publishing process
- SRE owns: runners/infra reliability, alert routing, on-call handoff, incident response mechanics
- Private Deployments/Installer eng owns: verification failure UX, support bundle contents, customer-facing troubleshooting steps

B) On-call expectations
- During release week: Release Eng is primary for signing pipeline failures; SRE secondary for infra issues.
- For customer verification failures during pilot: Support on-call engages first; SRE gets pulled in only if it looks systemic (bad artifact published / widespread failures).

C) Runbooks
We need three separate runbooks with explicit “owner” + “when to page”:
1) Signing pipeline failure runbook (Release Eng primary, SRE secondary)
2) Key rotation / trust store updates runbook (Release Eng + Security; includes customer comms steps)
3) Offline bundle verification failures runbook (Installer eng + Support), including where logs live, how to run the inspect command, and what to collect

I’ll add a small escalation tree diagram we can stick into the runbooks + pager payload (attached).

Attachment: oncall-escalation-tree-private-installer-signing.png

Sean
SRE Lead

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, Dec 12, 2025 at 11:22 AM
Subject: Re: Release gating + operational readiness for signed offline bundles (Redwood Private)

Security sanity check:

- +1 to fail closed by default (installer blocks install on invalid sig / unknown key / manifest mismatch).
- Break-glass must be policy-gated AND leave a durable audit trail locally. I want gating to include at least one test that ensures the audit marker is emitted when break-glass is used.
- Gating should block publish if the trust store / signing cert chain isn’t what we expect (we’ve had “works in staging” issues where a dev key slipped into a build).

On alerting: please make sure failures that are “key access denied” page immediately (that’s a custody/config drift issue and often indicates a permission change).

I’m available to review the final gating checklist and the pager payload text, so it’s consistent with what we tell customers during security reviews.

Marcus
Security Engineering

Subject: Re: Release gating + operational readiness for signed offline bundles (Redwood Private)

Locking decisions + actions:

1) Alerting (Owner: Sahana; Review: Connor + Sean)
- Paging only on signing job hard-fail / verification hard-fail / key access denied.
- Route: Release Eng primary; SRE secondary.
- Include runbook links + failure reason taxonomy in payload.
- Target: draft rules + dashboard by Tue 12/16; hook into ENG-4874.

2) Release gating (Owner: Connor; Security review: Marcus)
- Implement the “block cut” + “block publish” checks Connor outlined.
- Add explicit checks to prevent dev/staging key usage in prod artifacts.
- Ensure at least one CI test covers break-glass audit marker emission.
- Target: checklist in Confluence + wired into release train by end of week (ties to ENG-4862).

3) Runbooks (Owner assignments)
- Signing pipeline failure runbook: Connor (primary), Sean (secondary). Due: 12/18.
- Key rotation runbook: Connor + Marcus. Due: 12/19.
- Verification failures runbook: Sean + Dev Patel coordinating with installer team (Ethan to be pulled in separately). Due: 12/19.

4) On-call expectation (effective for pilot)
- Release week: Release Eng on-call is primary for signing pipeline pages.
- Support is first-line for customer verification failures; SRE engaged for systemic issues.

Talia—please capture these in the pilot readiness checklist and link to the runbooks once live.

If anything here is unrealistic, flag by EOD. Otherwise let’s execute.

Neha
